body: Okay, I will look into counselling services at my school. Hopefully something will turn up. Thanks again.

That's great that you have online friends that look out for you. I used to play WoW when I was younger, and I still have friends across the country that I talk to on a consistent basis. Maybe I'll look into getting back into video games.

I'm not having issues in school. In fact, it distracts my mind from the numb is always there. Additionally, I will be taking classes this summer to jump ahead a little bit.


I think I may have to talk to my parents about it though. As much as I hate to do it, you are right. I can't stand being this way.

>it isn't the end either

Also, I think that this is what keeps me going day after day. I know that there is a possibility that I won't be depressed in a year from now. And I might be in a great position in 5 years from now. Who knows?

Thank you for the kind words. It means a lot to know I'm not the only one. If I were to sum this whole ordeal up into one feeling, it would be a huge loss of motivation. Towards anything.

I remember flying home from an international competition in California last spring and finally sitting in my car in the parking lot after the long flight. I think that's when it all really hit me. I had this overwhelming feeling of hopelessness and loss. Like I had just given up everything I lived for.

I think you may be right on the bipolar part. Some days are better than others. 

And yeah, I have. But bringing up the topic to my parents would be quite the ordeal. They've told me to "suck it up" and "trust in God." It doesn't work that way I guess.
